verdicts.correction: The expected output (OPEN=00 LC=0001 / MAIN-W=00 LC=0002 / SUB-W=00 LC=0003 / AFTER-SUB LC=0003) is correct, and the clause numbers 13.18.34.4 7) d) and 7) c) 3. are the PRINTED ones. But header lines 16 and 20 record them as cite.py's output ('-> OK  §13.18.34.4 7) d)', '-> OK  §13.18.34.4 7) c) 3.'). cite.py --check actually prints '§13.18.34.4 7) a)' for both. That makes the header a false record of the mechanical check. Change them to the form the sibling goldens use: '-> OK  §13.18.34.4 7) d)  (printed under "7) a)")' and '-> OK  §13.18.34.4 7) c) 3.  (printed under "7) a)")', or record cite.py's verbatim label plus a note giving the printed item.

GR2 only constrains PROGRAMS: every FD of one external connector 'shall obey' a)-e). The writer concedes it has no mandated detection (§4.2.2). Everything the golden prints comes from §9.1.5 1) (one external connector: DX's WRITE without OPEN gives 00) and from GR-13.4.5.4-3 (external LINAGE-COUNTER 0001,0002 | 0002,0003 | 0004). An implementation with no notion of GR2 at all, neither checking nor using agreement, prints exactly the same lines. The witness is also redundant with conformance:85/l1c11_linage_counter_external_global. Fix: re-disposition the row as a constraint on the program, satisfied by construction and with no runtime-observable branch, and drop this golden from its test_ref. Alternatively point the row at a diagnostic test for the implementation's own CheckExternalFileConsistency, but only after documenting that detection as an implementor choice, since a mismatch is undefined, not a mandated rejection. Item e) is untested either way.

all_upheld_flag: Not all upheld (2 of 12 overturned). Checks: re-ran cite.py --check on all ~40 header citations; every clause number matched, except that cite.py mislabels 13.18.34.4 7)c)3./7)d) as 7)a), which the printed spec settles. Re-derived every .out by hand. SR-12.4.5.2: dynamic-mode out-of-order WRITEs (no status 21), dup 22, random READ then READ NEXT gives K2, K9 gives 23. GR-12.4.5.3-6: the 12.3.6.4 GR11 scope of PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE (comparisons only, not keys); AL-R order (a,Z,rest native) vs native code-unit order (DOC-A.1-8) for prime and alternate keys; START >= SPACES; national B<a<f<é, where the alternate map gives a1 é1 B1 f1; the DISPLAY-padding trap is covered because CompilerUnderTest.Normalize trims each line. LINAGE-COUNTER arithmetic against 13.18.34.4 7)c)/d) in three files; visibility of an unqualified LINAGE-COUNTER in contained and separately compiled programs. Table 19 cell by cell for both sharing goldens: an ALL OTHER EXTEND open against an existing ALL OTHER OUTPUT open is 'Normal open'; NO OTHER gives 61 both ways. EC-I-O-INVALID-KEY is NF (the exception table), so control returns after USE; the EXCEPTION-STATUS width is 31. Checked the constant-entry and TYPEDEF editions (2002) in constructs.json, the column lengths of the reference-format lines (72/80, text at column 73), and that each negative is legal apart from the one violation.
